assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wings and thorax but focuses on the speed of wing beats, not on describing outer body parts or identifying their role in movement or food gathering as required by G3-L-4. The content is tangentially related to wings but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How fast does a bee flap its wings?

Super fast! A bee's flight muscles are in its thorax and can beat its wings over 200 times every single second.
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis pumagaspas ang pakpak ng bubuyog?

Napakabilis! Ang kalamnan ng pakpak ng bubuyog ay nasa dibdib at nakakapagpapagaspas ng higit 200 beses sa loob lang ng isang segundo.
copy.bis:
Unsa kaspiid mopakpak ang pako sa buyog?

Paspas kaayo! Ang kaunuran sa pako sa buyog naa sa dughan ug makapakpak og labaw sa 200 ka beses matag segundo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they need little food, can hide in tiny spaces
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food and shelter as needs, but its focus is on why small size helps insects thrive, not on identifying the basic needs of all living things. It does not directly teach the concept of basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) as a general skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: can reproduce super fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions reproduction as one advantage of small size, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept. Reproduction is only cited as a benefit of being small, not taught as a characteristic of living things.

copy.en: Being small is a big reason insects thrive — they need little food, can hide in tiny spaces, and can reproduce super fast!
copy.tl: Ang maliit na sukat ng mga insekto ay isa sa dahilan ng kanilang tagumpay—kaunti lang ang kailangan nilang pagkain, kayang magtago sa maliliit na lugar, at mabilis silang dumami!
copy.bis: Ang gamay nga sukat sa mga insekto usa sa hinungdan sa ilang kalampusan—gamay lang ang ilang gikinahanglang pagkaon, makatago sila sa gagmay nga lugar, ug paspas sila modaghan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The special instrument that we use to measure temperature is called a thermometer!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan simple scientific investigations in answering questions, such as 'Do gases (like air) or liquids (like water) have mass?', using appropriate simple science equipment, such as a balance, and a thermometer, with appropriate units
assignedReviews.reason: The card only identifies the thermometer as the instrument for measuring temperature. The competency requires planning a scientific investigation (e.g., testing whether gases or liquids have mass) using equipment such as a balance and thermometer with appropriate units. The card provides no support for planning, measuring, or using units, and merely shares the vocabulary 'thermometer'.

copy.en:
What instrument do we use to measure temperature?

The special instrument that we use to measure temperature is called a thermometer!
copy.tl:
Anong instrumento ang ginagamit natin para sumukat ng temperatura?

Ang instrumentong ginagamit natin para sumukat ng temperatura ay tinatawag na thermometer, at napaka-gamit nito!
copy.bis:
Unsay instrumento nga atong gamiton aron mosukod sa temperatura?

Ang instrumento nga atong gamiton aron mosukod sa temperatura gitawag nga thermometer, ug kini mapuslanon kaayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: because it slows heat moving in either direction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that insulation slows heat transfer in either direction, but it does not identify or give examples of conduction, convection, or radiation, nor does it discuss advantages/disadvantages of those specific modes. It is only tangentially related to heat transfer.

copy.en:
Does insulation only work for keeping things warm?

The same insulation keeps hot things hot and cold things cold, because it slows heat moving in either direction!
copy.tl:
Para lang ba sa pagpapainit ang insulasyon?

Ang parehong insulasyon ay nagpapanatiling mainit ang mainit at malamig ang malamig, dahil pinapabagal nito ang init kahit anong direksyon!
copy.bis:
Para lang ba sa pagpapainit ang insulasyon?

Ang samang insulasyon magpabilin nga init sa init ug bugnaw sa bugnaw, kay magpahinay kini sa kainit bisan asa nga direksyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An insulator is a material that blocks electricity from flowing easily. Rubber and plastic are great examples of insulators!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an insulator and gives examples, which is background knowledge for identifying non-conducting materials. However, the competency requires designing and constructing a simple circuit to test materials; the card does not address circuit design, construction, or the testing process, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: An insulator is a material that blocks electricity from flowing easily. Rubber and plastic are great examples of insulators!
copy.tl: Ang insulador ay isang materyal na hindi nagpapadaloy ng kuryente nang madali. Ang goma at plastik ay mga halimbawa ng insulador!
copy.bis: Ang insulador usa ka materyal nga dili sayon nga paagian sa kuryente. Ang goma ug plastik maayong pananglitan sa insulador!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Insulators like rubber and plastic do not let electricity pass through
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about insulators but does not involve designing/constructing a circuit or using one to identify conducting/non-conducting materials, which is the core action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so they wrap around wires to keep us safe
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe and explain the need for safety precautions in handling household electrical devices
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions safety from electricity via insulation, but does not describe or explain safety precautions for handling household electrical devices, which is the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Insulators like rubber and plastic do not let electricity pass through
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses insulators blocking electricity but does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons nor explicitly address safe measures in handling electricity, so it only touches the same topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: materials like paper, wood, and plastic will not make the bulb light up because they are insulators
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses electrical insulators in a circuit, which is unrelated to drawing the structure of an atom in terms of nucleus and electron shells.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: materials like paper, wood, and plastic will not make the bulb light up because they are insulators
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses electrical insulators in a circuit, which is unrelated to differentiating subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons).

copy.en: In a circuit test, materials like paper, wood, and plastic will not make the bulb light up because they are insulators.
copy.tl: Sa pagsusuri ng circuit, ang mga materyales tulad ng papel, kahoy, at plastic ay hindi magpapailaw sa bombilya dahil sila ay mga insulators.
copy.bis: Sa pagsulay sa circuit, ang mga materyales sama sa papel, kahoy, ug plastic dili makapasiga sa bombilya tungod kay sila mga insulators.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An insulator is a material that does not let electricity flow through it!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an insulator and gives examples, which is background knowledge for the competency. However, the competency requires designing and constructing a simple circuit to identify conducting and non-conducting materials; the card does not support that investigative/design action.

copy.en:
What do we call a material that blocks electricity from flowing through it?

An insulator is a material that does not let electricity flow through it! Rubber and plastic are common examples.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa materyal na hindi nagpapadaloy ng kuryente?

Ang insulator ay materyal na hindi nagpapadaloy ng kuryente! Ang goma (rubber) at plastik ay karaniwang halimbawa.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa materyal nga dili magpaagi sa kuryente?

Ang insulator kay materyal nga dili magpaagi sa kuryente! Ang goma (rubber) ug plastik kasagaran nga pananglitan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Intermolecular forces are the pulls or pushes between molecules
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about intermolecular forces and states of matter, not weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, or humidity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Intermolecular forces are the pulls or pushes between molecules
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address locating or describing non-living things like rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, or sunlight; it is a chemistry topic on intermolecular forces.

copy.en: Intermolecular forces are the pulls or pushes between molecules, and they help decide whether a substance is a solid, liquid, or gas at room temperature.
copy.tl: Ang intermolecular forces ay ang mga paghila o pagtulak sa pagitan ng mga molecule, at nakakatulong sila para malaman kung ang isang substance ay solid, liquid, o gas sa room temperature.
copy.bis: Ang intermolecular forces mao ang mga pagbira o pagtulod tali sa mga molecule, ug makatabang kini aron mahibaloan kon ang usa ka substance solid, liquid, o gas sa room temperature.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The change in internal energy equals the heat added to a system minus the work done by the system.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances, such as melting point, hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the first law of thermodynamics (internal energy change), which is physics. G9-M-11 requires investigating properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances (melting point, hardness, conductivity). The card provides no support for that competency.

copy.en: The change in internal energy equals the heat added to a system minus the work done by the system.
copy.tl: Ang pagbabago sa internal energy ay katumbas ng init na idinagdag sa system minus ang work na ginawa ng system.
copy.bis: Ang kausaban sa internal energy katumbas sa init nga gidugang sa system minus ang work nga gihimo sa system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a band near the equator where winds from the north and south meet and rise!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes what the ITCZ is and its effect (clouds and rain) but does not explain how solar energy contributes to its occurrence, which is the core action of the competency. It provides background knowledge about the ITCZ but not the required causal explanation involving solar energy.

copy.en:
What is the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?

It's a band near the equator where winds from the north and south meet and rise! It cools down, bringing thick clouds and heavy rain to the Philippines.
copy.tl:
Ano ang Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?

Ito ay isang banda malapit sa ekwador kung saan nagtatagpo at umaakyat ang hangin mula sa hilaga at timog! Lumalamig ito, kaya nagdadala ng makapal na ulap at malakas na ulan sa Pilipinas.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?

Usa kini ka banda duol sa ekwador diin magtagbo ug mosaka ang hangin gikan sa amihanan ug habagatan! Mobugnaw kini, mao nga magdala og baga nga panganod ug kusog nga ulan sa Pilipinas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Worms are more common where clean water and toilets are scarce
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions worms and lack of clean water/toilets, but it does not explain an interaction between living and non-living things bringing good or harm. It is a hygiene/sanitation observation, not an ecosystem interaction lesson.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Worms are more common where clean water and toilets are scarce
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on water and sanitation but does not identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It is about worm prevalence and deworming, not a lesson on basic needs.

copy.en: Worms are more common where clean water and toilets are scarce, especially in the countryside — that's why the government gives free deworming medicine to schoolchildren.
copy.tl: Mas madalas ang bulati kung saan kulang ang malinis na tubig at palikuran, lalo na sa probinsya — kaya nagbibigay ang gobyerno ng libreng purga sa mga bata sa paaralan.
copy.bis: Mas komon ang bulati kung diin kulang ang limpyo nga tubig ug kasilyas, ilabi na sa probinsya — mao nga naghatag ang gobyerno og libreng purga sa mga bata sa eskwelahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooking food well kills the worm eggs and larvae that might be inside it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cooking, which involves heat, but it does not identify or describe conduction, convection, or radiation, nor any advantageous/disadvantageous examples of these heat transfer modes. It is a food-safety statement about killing worm eggs, not instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooking food well kills the worm eggs and larvae that might be inside it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves a temperature-related change (cooking kills eggs/larvae), but it does not describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes, such as burning wood or coal. It is about biological contamination, not material property changes.

copy.en: Cooking food well kills the worm eggs and larvae that might be inside it.
copy.tl: Ang mabuting pagluluto ng pagkain ay pumapatay sa itlog at larva ng bulate na maaaring nasa loob nito.
copy.bis: Ang maayong pagluto sa pagkaon makapatay sa itlog ug larva sa bulate nga mahimong anaa sa sulod niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tiny worm eggs can sneak into your body and grow into worms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses worm infection via unwashed food and dirty water, but does not identify or describe any parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or how they work. It is unrelated to the competency's subject.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: grow into worms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions worms growing, which touches on the characteristic of growth, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept. The focus is on infection, not on teaching that living things grow, respond, and reproduce.

copy.en:
How can you catch worms from food?

If you eat unwashed vegetables or fruit, or drink dirty water, tiny worm eggs can sneak into your body and grow into worms!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakahawa ng bulate ang pagkain?

Kapag kumain ka ng hindi hugasang gulay o prutas, o uminom ng maruming tubig, puwedeng makapasok sa katawan mo ang itlog ng bulate at lumaki doon!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkuha og bulate gikan sa pagkaon?

Kon mokaon ka og utanon o prutas nga wala hugasi, o moinom og hugaw nga tubig, mahimong makasulod sa imong lawas ang itlog sa bulate ug motubo didto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most invasive species are brought in by people
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how invasive species are introduced by human activities (purposeful or accidental), but the competency requires describing the possible effects of such human activities on living things in an ecosystem. The card does not address any effects, only the arrival mechanism, so it is related background rather than direct support.

copy.en: Most invasive species are brought in by people — sometimes on purpose, like for food or pets, and sometimes by accident, like riding along on a ship.
copy.tl: Karamihan sa invasive species ay dala ng tao — minsan sinasadya gaya ng pagkain o alagang hayop, at minsan aksidente gaya ng pagsakay sa barko.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa invasive species gidala sa tao — usahay tinuyo sama sa pagkaon o binuhi nga hayop, ug usahay aksidente sama sa pagsakay sa barko.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it clogs canals, irrigation channels, and water pumps — water struggles to reach farms or power plants, so a lot of money must be spent clearing it out.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an invasive species (water hyacinth) and an effect, but the effect described is on human infrastructure (canals, pumps) and economic cost, not on living things in an ecosystem. The competency requires describing effects of human activities (including introduction of invasive species) on living things. No living things other than the water hyacinth are mentioned, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it clogs canals, irrigation channels, and water pumps — water struggles to reach farms or power plants, so a lot of money must be spent clearing it out.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an interaction between a living thing (water hyacinth) and non-living things (canals, water pumps, water flow), but the harm described is economic and infrastructural, not harm to living things involved. The competency requires explaining how interactions bring good or harm to the living things involved. The card does not explain harm to any living thing; it only mentions cost and water reaching farms/power plants, which are human concerns. Thus it is related but not direct.

copy.en: When water hyacinth piles up, it clogs canals, irrigation channels, and water pumps — water struggles to reach farms or power plants, so a lot of money must be spent clearing it out.
copy.tl: Kapag dumami ang water hyacinth, bumabara ito sa mga kanal, patubig, at mga makinang kumukuha ng tubig — nahihirapang dumaloy ang tubig papunta sa bukid o planta ng kuryente, kaya nadadagdagan ang gastos sa paglilinis.
copy.bis: Kon modaghan ang water hyacinth, mobara kini sa mga kanal, patubig, ug mga makina nga magkuha og tubig — maglisod ang tubig pag-agos ngadto sa uma o planta sa kuryente, busa daghang gasto sa paghinlo niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Invasive species spread fast because their new home often has no natural enemies, diseases, or rivals to hold them back — so their numbers explode.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why invasive species spread quickly (lack of natural enemies, diseases, rivals), but it does not describe the possible effects of human activities such as deforestation, pollution, or introduction of invasive species on living things in an ecosystem. It shares the topic of invasive species but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Invasive species spread fast because their new home often has no natural enemies, diseases, or rivals to hold them back — so their numbers explode.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the factors that limit the ecosystem's carrying capacity, such as adequate food, shelter, water, and mates
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses population explosion of invasive species, which is tangentially related to carrying capacity, but it does not discuss factors that limit an ecosystem's carrying capacity such as adequate food, shelter, water, and mates. No direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why do invasive species spread so fast?

Invasive species spread fast because their new home often has no natural enemies, diseases, or rivals to hold them back — so their numbers explode.
copy.tl:
Bakit mabilis kumalat ang invasive species?

Mabilis kumalat ang invasive species dahil sa bagong lugar, kadalasang walang natural na kaaway, sakit, o katunggali na pipigil sa kanila — kaya mabilis silang dumami.
copy.bis:
Nganong paspas mokatag ang invasive species?

Paspas mokatag ang invasive species kay sa bag-ong dapit, kasagaran walay natural nga kaaway, sakit, o kakompetensya nga mopugong nila — busa paspas silang modaghan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they include hugely different body shapes, from insects and spiders to snails, sea stars, and jellyfish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Varied invertebrate body plans do not describe backbone versus no backbone.

copy.en: Invertebrates are not just one kind — they include hugely different body shapes, from insects and spiders to snails, sea stars, and jellyfish.
copy.tl: Ang mga invertebrate ay hindi iisang uri lamang — kasama dito ang napakaraming magkakaibang anyo, mula sa insekto at gagamba hanggang sa kuhol, bituing-dagat, at dikya.
copy.bis: Ang mga invertebrate dili usa ra ka matang — apil dinhi ang daghan kaayong lainlaing dagway, gikan sa insekto ug lawalawa hangtod sa kuhol, bituon sa dagat, ug bukya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not enough iodine in your food can cause goiter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses iodine deficiency and goiter, a nutrition/health topic. It does not teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) as a general concept, so it only shares the broad subject of food/nutrition without directly supporting the competency.

copy.en:
Why does salt have added iodine?

Not enough iodine in your food can cause goiter — that's why iodized salt is so important.
copy.tl:
Bakit may idinadagdag na iodine sa asin?

Ang kakulangan sa iodine ay maaaring magdulot ng goiter — kaya mahalaga ang asing may iodine.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga adunay gidugang nga iodine sa asin?

Ang kakulang sa yodo mahimong hinungdan sa goiter — mao nga importante ang asin nga adunay yodo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Iodine, found in iodized salt and seafood, is needed by the body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses iodine as a nutrient preventing goiter, which is a specific human health topic. It does not address the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter) as required by G3-L-6. The content is unrelated to the competency's subject.

copy.en:
Why does the body need iodine?

Iodine, found in iodized salt and seafood, is needed by the body — without enough, it can cause goiter, a swelling in the neck.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng katawan ang iodine?

Kailangan ng katawan ang iodine, na matatagpuan sa iodized salt at isda; ang kakulangan nito ay maaaring magdulot ng goiter, o pamamaga sa leeg.
copy.bis:
Nganong gikinahanglan sa lawas ang iodine?

Gikinahanglan sa lawas ang iodine, nga makita sa iodized salt ug isda; ang kakulang niini mahimong hinungdan sa goiter, o paghubag sa liog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: too much iodine can also harm your thyroid, so your body needs just the right amount
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a need for the right amount of iodine, which is a balance concept, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor mention the indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure). It is a specific nutrient example, not direct instruction on the homeostasis competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body needs just the right amount, which a balanced diet usually gives
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a balanced diet, which relates to food as a basic need, but it does not identify the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It focuses on iodine intake, not the general concept of basic needs.

copy.en: More isn't always better — too much iodine can also harm your thyroid, so your body needs just the right amount, which a balanced diet usually gives.
copy.tl: Hindi laging mas mabuti ang mas marami — ang sobrang iodine ay pwede ring makasama sa thyroid, kaya tamang-tama lang ang kailangan, na karaniwang nakukuha na sa balanseng pagkain.
copy.bis: Dili kanunay mas maayo ang sobra — ang sobrang iodine makadaot usab sa thyroid, mao nga ang lawas nagkinahanglan lang og husto nga gidaghanon, nga sagad naa na sa balanseng pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it helps protect people from getting goiter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why iodine is added to salt (to prevent goiter). It does not address identifying basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Why is iodine added to salt in the Philippines?

Many salt brands in the Philippines add iodine (iodized salt) because it helps protect people from getting goiter.
copy.tl:
Bakit may yodo ang maraming asin sa Pilipinas?

Maraming asin sa Pilipinas ang nilalagyan ng yodo dahil nakakatulong ito na maiwasan ang goiter sa mga tao.
copy.bis:
Nganong adunay yodo ang daghang asin sa Pilipinas?

Daghang asin sa Pilipinas ang gidugangan ug yodo kay makatabang kini nga malikayan ang goiter sa mga tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its sturdy wood is used for building houses and furniture
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a tree and its wood as a building material, but does not address how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It is only tangentially about a living thing.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its sturdy wood is used for building houses and furniture
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency concerns useful things made from non-living materials. Wood comes from a living tree, not a non-living material, so the card does not directly support identifying useful items made from non-living materials.

copy.en:
Is your blood magnetic because of iron?

Nope! Your blood does have iron, but it's a tiny amount locked inside hemoglobin — not enough to make you magnetic or stick to a fridge.
copy.tl:
Magnetic ba ang dugo mo dahil may iron?

Hindi pala! May iron nga sa dugo mo, pero napakaliit lang ng dami nito at nakatali sa hemoglobin — hindi ito sapat para maging magnetic ka o kumapit sa ref.
copy.bis:
Magnetic ba ang imong dugo tungod sa iron?

Dili diay! Aduna gyoy iron sa imong dugo, apan gamay ra kaayo ug nahigot sa sulod sa hemoglobin — dili kini igo aron mahimo kang magnetic o mopilit sa ref.

copy.tl: Kailangan ng utak ng buto ang bakal bilang sangkap para makagawa ng bagong pulang selula na may hemoglobin.
copy.bis: Ang kinauyokan sa bukog nagkinahanglan og puthaw isip sangkap aron makahimo og bag-ong pula nga selula nga adunay hemoglobin.

How do crops get water when there's no rain?

Through irrigation! It's a system of canals and pipes that brings water from a river or dam to the fields to water the crops.
copy.tl:
Paano nabibigyan ng tubig ang mga pananim kapag walang ulan?

Sa pamamagitan ng irrigation! Ito ay sistema ng mga canal at pipes na nagdadala ng tubig mula sa ilog o dam patungo sa bukid para diligan ang pananim.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghatag ug tubig sa mga tanom kung walay ulan?

Pinaagi sa irrigation! Kini usa ka sistema sa mga canal ug pipes nga nagdala ug tubig gikan sa suba o dam ngadto sa uma aron mabisbisan ang mga tanom.

What makes isotopes of the same element different from each other?

They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, like carbon-12 and carbon-14!

Ano ang nagpapaiba sa mga isotopo ng parehong elemento?

May parehong bilang ng proton sila ngunit magkaibang bilang ng neutron, gaya ng carbon-12 at carbon-14!

Unsay nagpakalahi sa mga isotope sa samang elemento?

Adunay parehong gidaghanon sa proton apan lahi ang gidaghanon sa neutron, sama sa carbon-12 ug carbon-14!

What are isotopes?

They are different versions of the same element with the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons, like carbon-12 and carbon-14!

Ano ang mga isotope?

Ito ay magkakaibang bersyon ng iisang element na may parehong bilang ng proton pero magkaibang bilang ng neutron, gaya ng carbon-12 at carbon-14!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mga isotope?

Kini ang lain-laing bersyon sa usa ra ka element nga may managsama nga gidaghanon sa proton apan lahi og gidaghanon sa neutron, sama sa carbon-12 ug carbon-14!

Jackfruit; it is sweet when ripe and holds many seeds inside.

Ang langka; ito ay matamis kapag hinog at may maraming buto sa loob.

Unsa ang pinakadakong prutas nga motubo sa kahoy?

Ang nangka; tam-is kini kon hinog ug daghan og liso sa sulod.

Why is the inside of a jackfruit seed so thick?

That thick inside is a food store the tiny baby plant uses while it's just starting to sprout.
copy.tl:
Bakit makapal ang loob ng buto ng langka?

Ang makapal na laman ng buto ng langka ay tindahan ng pagkain na ginagamit ng maliit na halaman habang sumisibol pa lang ito.
copy.bis:
Nganong baga ang sulod sa liso sa nangka?

Ang baga nga sulod sa liso sa nangka maoy tipiganan sa pagkaon nga gamiton sa gamay nga tanom samtang nag-ugbos pa lang kini.

copy.en:
What does cooked jackfruit seed taste like?

Once cooked, a jackfruit seed tastes a bit like chestnut or potato — soft and slightly sweet.
copy.tl:
Ano ang lasa ng nilutong buto ng langka?

Kapag niluto na, ang buto ng langka ay parang kastanyas o patatas ang lasa — malambot at bahagyang matamis.
copy.bis:
Unsay lami sa lutô nga liso sa nangka?

Kung maluto na, ang liso sa nangka morag chestnut o patatas ang lami — humok ug medyo tam-is.

copy.bis: Ang matag liso sa nangka anaa sa sulod sa iyahang kaugalingong tam-is ug dalag nga pod, busa ang matag pod adunay kaugalingong liso.

copy.en: Inside a jackfruit are many yellow pods, each with its own seed — a big jackfruit can hold hundreds of seeds!
copy.tl: Sa loob ng langka ay maraming dilaw na laman, bawat isa'y may sariling buto — makakaabot pa sa daan-daang buto ang isang malaking langka!
copy.bis: Sa sulod sa nangka daghan ang dilaw nga unod, matag usa adunay kaugalingong liso — makaabot pa og gatusan ka liso ang usa ka dako nga nangka!

How many fruits can one jackfruit tree grow yearly?

About 200! A mature jackfruit tree can produce around 200 fruits in just one year.
copy.tl:
Ilang prutas ang kayang ibunga ng isang puno ng langka?

Mga 200! Ang isang ganap na puno ng langka ay maaaring mamunga ng mga 200 prutas sa loob ng isang taon.
copy.bis:
Pila ka prutas ang mahatag sa usa ka kahoy sa nangka?

Mga 200! Ang usa ka hamtong nga kahoy sa nangka makapamunga og mga 200 ka prutas sulod sa usa ka tuig.

How heavy can a jackfruit get?

A single jackfruit can weigh up to about 50 kilograms — as heavy as a young child!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabigat ang pinakamalaking langka?

Ang isang langka ay maaaring tumimbang ng hanggang 50 kilo — kasinbigat ng isang batang tao!
copy.bis:
Unsa kabug-at ang labing dako nga nangka?

Ang usa ka nangka mahimong mobug-at og hangtod sa 50 ka kilo — sama kabug-at sa usa ka bata!

Why is the janitor fish called that?

People once kept it in aquariums to clean algae off the glass — but once released into rivers, it became invasive!

Bakit tinawag itong janitor fish?

Dahil inaalagaan ito noon sa akwaryum para linisin ang lumot sa salamin — pero nang mapalaya sa mga ilog, naging invasive ito!
copy.bis:
Ngano gitawag kining janitor fish?

Kaniadto gibuhi kini sa akwaryum aron limpyohan ang lumot sa salamin — apan sa dihang nabuhian sa mga suba, nahimo kining invasive!

Can a jellyfish swim far on its own?

Not really! A jellyfish mostly drifts along with the ocean's currents and waves — that's why you often see it floating in the water.

Kaya bang lumangoy nang malayo ng dikya?

Hindi talaga! Naaanod lamang ang dikya kasama ng agos at alon ng dagat — kaya madalas mo itong makitang lutaw-lutaw sa tubig.
copy.bis:
Makahimo ba ang dikya og layo nga paglangoy?

Dili gyud! Ang dikya anod-anod lang kuyog sa sulog ug balod sa dagat — mao nga kanunay nimo kini makita nga naglutaw sa tubig.

Why do jellyfish glow in the dark?

Some jellyfish make their own light in the dark ocean — it's called bioluminescence, and they use it to startle or confuse their enemies!
copy.tl:
Bakit nagliliwanag ang dikya sa dilim?

May mga dikya na gumagawa ng sarili nilang liwanag sa dilim ng dagat — tinatawag itong bioluminescence, at ginagamit nila ito para takutin o lituhin ang mga kaaway!
copy.bis:
Nganong nagsidlak ang dikya sa ngitngit?

Ang ubang dikya maghimo sa ilang kaugalingong kahayag sa ngitngit nga dagat — gitawag kini og bioluminescence, ug gigamit nila kini aron kuratan o libgon ang mga kaaway!

How does a jellyfish breathe without lungs?

A jellyfish has no blood and no lungs — oxygen just seeps straight from the water into its thin body, so it never needs to breathe like we do!
copy.tl:
Paano huminga ang dikya kahit walang baga?

Ang dikya ay walang dugo at walang baga — dumadaan lang ang oxygen mula sa tubig papasok sa manipis nitong katawan, kaya hindi na kailangang huminga tulad natin!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagginhawa sa dikya kung walay baga?

Ang dikya walay dugo ug walay baga — mosulod lang ang oksiheno gikan sa tubig diretso sa nipis niini nga lawas, mao nga dili gyud kini kinahanglan moginhawa sama nato!

Nakakaramdam ba ang dikya kahit walang utak?

Oo! May magkakawing na mga nerbiyo ang dikya na kumakalat sa buong katawan nito, tinatawag na nerve net, na nagpaparamdam dito ng hipo at liwanag para agad tumugon.

Makabati ba ang dikya bisan walay utok?

Oo! Adunay nagkadugtong nga mga nerbiyo ang dikya nga nagkatag sa tibuok lawas niini, gitawag og nerve net, nga makapabati niini sa hikap ug kahayag aron dali motubag.

copy.en:
Jellyfish sting — what should you rinse with?

If a jellyfish stings you, it's better to rinse with seawater instead of fresh water.
copy.tl:
Napaso ka ng dikya, ano ang gagawin?

Kapag napaso ka ng dikya, mas mabuting banlawan ito ng tubig-dagat kaysa tubig-tabang.
copy.bis:
Napaso ka sa dikya, unsay buhaton?

Kon mapaso ka sa dikya, mas maayong hugasan kini og tubig-dagat kaysa tubig-tabang.

copy.bis: Kon matusok ka sa dikya, hugasi kini og tubig-dagat o suka ug ayaw kuskusa sa imong kamot — sultihi dayon ang usa ka hamtong aron matabangan ka.

What is the jet stream way up in the sky?

The jet stream is a super-fast ribbon of wind high in the atmosphere! It steers weather systems and can even speed up airplanes flying along with it!
copy.tl:
Ano ang jet stream sa napakataas na bahagi ng langit?

Ang jet stream ay napakabilis na agos ng hangin sa mataas na bahagi ng atmosphere! Ginagabayan nito ang mga sistema ng panahon at pinapabilis ang mga eroplanong sumasabay sa daloy nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang jet stream sa taas kaayo nga bahin sa langit?

Ang jet stream usa ka paspas kaayo nga agos sa hangin sa habog nga bahin sa atmosphere! Giyahan niini ang mga sistema sa panahon ug gipaspas ang mga ayroplano nga mosakay niini!

Did a comet ever crash into Jupiter?

Yes! In 1994, comet Shoemaker–Levy 9 broke into pieces and crashed into Jupiter, leaving big dark marks that telescopes on Earth could see!

Oo! Noong 1994, ang kometa na Shoemaker–Levy 9 ay nahati at bumangga sa Jupiter, nag-iwan ng malalaking itim na marka na nakita ng mga teleskopyo sa Earth!
copy.bis:
Nakabangga ba gyud ang usa ka kometa sa Jupiter?

Oo! Niadtong 1994, ang kometa nga Shoemaker–Levy 9 nabuak ug nibangga sa Jupiter, nagbilin og dagkong itom nga marka nga nakita sa mga teleskopyo sa Earth!

How does Jupiter protect Earth?

Jupiter’s strong gravity pulls comets and asteroids away from the inner solar system! Scientists call it a 'shield' that helps protect Earth from space collisions.
copy.tl:
Paano pinoprotektahan ng Jupiter ang Earth?

Hinihila ng malakas na gravity ng Jupiter ang mga kometa at asteroid palayo! Tinatawag itong 'kalasag' ng mga siyentista na nakakatulong protektahan ang Earth sa banggaan.
copy.bis:
Unsaon sa Jupiter sa panalipdan ang Earth?

Ginabira sa kusog nga gravity sa Jupiter ang mga kometa ug asteroid palayo! Gitawag kini sa mga siyentista nga 'taming' nga makatabang panalipdan sa Earth gikan sa banggaan.

Why is the James Webb Space Telescope hard to repair?

Unlike the close Hubble, James Webb sits 1.5 million kilometers away—farther than the Moon! This huge distance makes it very hard to repair if it breaks.
copy.tl:
Bakit mahirap ayusin ang James Webb Space Telescope?

Hindi tulad ng malapit na Hubble, ang James Webb ay nasa layong 1.5 milyong kilometro—mas malayo pa sa Buwan! Kaya napakahirap nitong ayusin kung masira.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga lisod ayohon ang James Webb Space Telescope?

Dili sama sa duol nga Hubble, ang James Webb naa sa gilay-on nga 1.5 milyon ka kilometro—mas layo pa kay sa Bulan! Mao nga lisod kaayo kini ayohon kon maguba.
